A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, framework, datasets and principal analyses. All pages, figures, equations and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data optimization experiments, trained-RNN comparisons and analyses of neural recordings, including Figures 2–7 and S1–S2.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and additionally reports RSA relationship results in Figure S5 and detailed denoising evidence in Figure S3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1 and C.1 revise the written ridge-similarity optimization target: regularization affects coefficient fitting but no longer contributes directly to the resulting score. An implementation change is not established. The overall Adam-based framework remains; Appendix C.3's explicit absolute-error loss documents the existing joint-optimization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the five neural datasets, their decision-making, reaching and visual tasks, and the synthetic/Gaussian analyses. The added RSA comparisons specify no additional dataset, population or task; their reference dataset is not identified.

E2.justification: Figure S5 adds evaluated RSA variants using Euclidean dissimilarity matrices with cosine similarity, centered cosine similarity and correlation. These are compared with CKA and with one another. Existing similarity measures, RNN architectures and neuron-split/condition-average baselines remain.

E3.justification: The reported ridge evaluation changes from including the regularization penalty in R2 to computing residual-only R2 after regularized fitting. This revises the stated scoring protocol without establishing reruns. Existing cross-validation and decoding procedures remain; Appendix B.1 primarily supplies previously undisclosed preprocessing settings.

E4.justification: Figure S3 supplies detailed evidence for the low-variance-PC denoising check already described in v2 Section 4.1. Figure S5 adds analyses of how RSA centering and RDM comparison choices affect relationships between scores. Existing variance-sensitivity and regularization analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures. Existing uncertainty displays are retained, and the new supplementary results introduce no additional statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Results in Figures 1–7 and S1–S2 are retained. Figure S3 adds denoising curves supporting the earlier observation. Figure S5 newly reports CKA equivalence with centered-cosine RSA, largely independent relationships with other RSA variants, and non-equivalence between cosine- and correlation-based RSA.

T1.justification: The regression-score definition is corrected by separating penalized coefficient estimation from residual-based R2 in Sections 3.1 and C.1. The CKA/NBS perturbation derivation and assumptions in Appendix C.2 remain unchanged; removing 'Proof' from its heading does not remove the derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and five enumerated contributions retain the same central claims about task-information encoding, dataset-dependent score interpretation, PC sensitivity, theoretical relationships and allowable score ranges. The added appendix evidence does not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: The discussion replaces the explicit qualification that no metric is superior with practical guidance to interpret scores through task-variable decodability and the PCs captured. The differentiability and optimizer-confounding limitations remain. Figure S3 elaborates the existing denoising interpretation without establishing a new mechanism.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 expands brief dataset descriptions into condition/trial and neuron counts, averaging procedures, time windows, bin widths and final tensor dimensions. It discloses 99%-variance PCA retention for Mante and Siegel. Appendix C.3 and Figure S4 additionally specify the absolute-error objective and achievable-boundary construction, substantially expanding reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds the RSA reference by Kriegeskorte et al. (2008a) and Williams (2024), and removes Cloos et al. (2024). Section 2 sharpens the positioning around interpreting intermediate similarity scores, contrasting this with invariance properties at maximum similarity.

P1.justification: Local revisions clarify score interpretation, PC thresholds, perturbations and joint optimization, alongside paragraph consolidation and expanded appendix descriptions. The title, overall section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures S3–S5: denoising evidence, an explanation of joint-score boundary estimation, and RSA comparisons. Figure 5 receives clearer axis and color-bar labels. Existing principal figures and the overall document layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Detailed preprocessing information, explicit joint-optimization instructions, revised regression-score mathematics and Figures S3–S5 make the work easier to scrutinize and reproduce. The gains supplement an otherwise stable paper. Some ambiguity remains: B.1's PCA preprocessing is not reconciled with B.2's statement that scores precede dimensionality reduction, and S5 leaves its reference dataset unspecified.
